input: Apply for a local arts council micro-grant

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing what the grant is specifically for (a project, event, purchase, etc.) determines what needs to be written, budgeted, and justified in the application.
The deadline and current application window directly affect how urgent the plan needs to be and whether there is time for revision or feedback.
Whether this is an individual artist, a group, or an organisation changes eligibility requirements, who signs the application, and how supporting materials are assembled.
The grant amount being sought and any budget ceiling shapes how the financial section is written and what project scale is feasible to propose.
Knowing whether the application is online, paper-based, or requires specific attachments determines the immediate next action and workflow.
Understanding the user's experience with grant writing reveals whether they need step-by-step guidance or just a checklist, and how much support to build into the plan.
Clarifying what a strong application looks like to the user — funded on first try, a learning experience, or meeting a specific panel criterion — sets the bar for quality and effort.

gold.taskTitle: Apply for a local arts council micro-grant
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to successfully submit an application for a micro-grant from their local arts council to fund an arts-related project or activity.

questions.title: What specific project or activity will this grant fund?
questions.description: Identify the exact creative project, event, equipment purchase, or activity the grant money will support, so the application narrative and budget can be built around it.

questions.title: When is the application deadline for this grant?
questions.description: Pin down the exact submission date or current open window so the plan can be sequenced with enough time for drafting, review, and submission.

questions.title: Are you applying as an individual artist or an organisation?
questions.description: Determine the applicant type to ensure eligibility requirements are met and the correct supporting documentation (e.g. ABN, incorporation papers, CV) is prepared.

questions.title: How much funding are you requesting from this grant?
questions.description: Establish the target grant amount so the budget breakdown can be planned appropriately and checked against the micro-grant funding ceiling.

questions.title: Is the application submitted online, by post, or another way?
questions.description: Identify the exact submission format and platform so the correct file types, word limits, and form fields can be prepared in advance.

questions.title: How much grant-writing experience do you have so far?
questions.description: Gauge the user's familiarity with grant applications to calibrate whether the plan should include detailed writing guidance, templates, or just a high-level checklist.

questions.title: What would a successful outcome look like to you?
questions.description: Understand whether the priority is winning the grant, building skills, meeting a specific assessment criterion, or something else, so the plan focuses effort in the right direction.
